reason: The cited evidence supports Y₂O₃-induced grain refinement and room-temperature strengthening in a NiCoCr superalloy (E1) and dispersion strengthening with high-temperature improvements in NiCoCr MPEA (E2), but neither study involves a Ti–Ni HEA or tests at 800–1000 °C, leaving the key premise of applicability to this specific system unsupported.
premises: Y₂O₃ nanoparticles can be uniformly incorporated into a metallic matrix via powder decoration and consolidation
Y₂O₃ nanoparticles refine grain size in the alloy
Y₂O₃ nanoparticles provide dispersion strengthening by impeding dislocations and pinning grain boundaries
These microstructural changes enhance elevated-temperature strength and creep resistance
The cited effects are applicable to a Ti–Ni HEA system
